fin.role: the lane's code tip: serve --prewarm and the join lookahead

pre3.role: the last build before index format 3, which loaded the unsegmented stores db10m-u and db1m-u

exp.role: base with an uncommitted first version of the join lookahead and an XNOLOOK environment switch that turns it off, used only for look-agg

att1.role: the final code: 38deb1e8 with the lookahead's first look and walk kept out of line and cold

compiler_provenance: GCC 15.3.0, clang 23.1.0git, LLD 23.1.1, rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13); the .comment sections of the five binaries are identical. Built on forge with mbx build --release -p sparkles-server --bin sparkles in nix develop.
stores: db10m and db1m are format 3 stores loaded by base from the synthetic generator at 10.5M and 1.05M triples; db10m-u and db1m-u are unsegmented stores loaded by pre3.
locks: Every step held ~/lanes/.heavy.lock on forge; no other build or benchmark ran during a step.

methods.ab: scripts/ab.sh: interleaved rounds of A, B, B and A, each a bench-regressions.py run with --cold N (a fresh server per sample after evicting the store with posix_fadvise DONTNEED) or --warmup 3 and N warm samples, server pinned to CPUs 0-11, port 43800.
methods.prewarm: bench-regressions.py --prewarm: a seed pass per query records prewarm.json from a warm server, the list is restored before each sample, and each cold sample starts a server with --prewarm and waits for its 'prewarm finished' log line before the query; ready_ms and prewarm_ms are kept per sample.
methods.insn: scripts/insn.sh: a warm server per binary and round, three warm-up requests per query, then perf stat -e instructions:u on the server process over 20 requests. scripts/insn.sh in this record points perf at a GC root; the first insn step used the same perf build from the store directly.
methods.engines: scripts/plan3.sh: scripts/bench.sh MODE=cold COLD_RUNS=5 SKIP_LOAD=1 for Oxigraph from the repository's pinned packages, fin and base, in two rounds per scale with the engines in turn.
methods.fe: scripts/fe.sh: a warm server per binary and round, three warm-up requests, then perf stat over 20 requests with user-mode cycles, instructions, frontend_retired.any_dsb_miss, frontend_retired.l1i_miss, frontend_retired.itlb_miss, dsb2mite_switches.penalty_cycles, br_misp_retired.all_branches, topdown-fe-bound and slots on the P-cores.

steps.suite10: base against fin, 28 queries, 10.5M, 7 cold samples, 2 pairs
steps.suite1: base against fin, 28 queries, 1.05M, 7 cold samples, 1 pair
steps.unseg-fin: pre3 on the unsegmented store against fin on format 3, 10.5M, 11 cold samples, 2 pairs
steps.prewarm10: fin against fin with --prewarm, 10.5M, 7 cold samples, 1 pair
steps.prewarm1: fin against fin with --prewarm, 1.05M, 7 cold samples, 1 pair
steps.warm10: base against fin, 27 queries without export, 10.5M, 21 warm samples, 2 pairs
steps.flag10: base against fin, the queries suite10 flagged, 10.5M, 11 cold samples, 3 pairs
steps.flag1: base against fin, the queries suite1 flagged, 1.05M, 11 cold samples, 3 pairs
steps.look-agg: exp with XNOLOOK=1 against exp, 10.5M, 7 cold samples, 2 pairs
steps.prof-base-agg, prof-fin-agg: profile=io of group-avg, expr-agg-arg, values-star and path-plus, 3 cold samples
steps.bench-<scale>-<engine>-<round>: bench.sh cold rows of five queries
steps.fe1: front-end counters of base, fin and att1, 2 rounds
steps.att1-warm: base against att1, 5 queries, 10.5M, 21 warm samples, 2 pairs
steps.att1-cold: base against att1, 5 queries, 10.5M, 11 cold samples, 2 pairs
steps.att1-suite10: base against att1, 28 queries, 10.5M, 7 cold samples, 2 pairs
steps.att1-warm10: base against att1, 27 queries, 10.5M, 21 warm samples, 2 pairs
steps.att1-warmflag: base against att1, the queries att1-warm10 flagged and the two placement queries, 10.5M, 21 warm samples, 4 pairs
steps.insn-att1: instructions per request of base, fin and att1, 2 rounds

correctness: Every A/B step's summary lists one answer hash per query across both sides (column 'hashes'). bench.sh checks row agreement across the engines before timing.
